explanation.headline: Insufficient net delta‑v left the vehicle with a low perigee
explanation.why: The vehicle delivered only 7717 m/s of delta‑v while the ideal requirement was 9308 m/s; losses of 894 m/s to gravity, 242 m/s to drag and 181 m/s to steering in Stage 1 (plus smaller losses in Stage 2) removed about 1591 m/s, leaving insufficient velocity to raise perigee above the ~150 km re‑entry threshold, resulting in a perigee of 141.4 km and apogee of 156.6 km instead of the 500 km circular target.

99001-61740.policy_text: Manoeuvre when Pc >= 1e-4 and a verified option exists. Between 1e-5 and 1e-4, or when Pc is diluted, prefer getting precise data if there is time before the latest safe burn. On public TLE data, do not decide a burn while there is time to get precise ephemeris; TLE screening finds candidates, it does not decide manoeuvres. Never manoeuvre if our propulsion status is unverified. If the other object is an active satellite that can manoeuvre, contact its operator before moving; if it is an operational satellite whose capability is unknown, notify its operator. Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.

decision.rationale: Pc is 5.3e-05, which lies between the operator's yellow (1e-5) and red (1e-4) thresholds. With ample time (>140 h) until TCA and before the latest safe burn (O2 at 2026-11-02T05:08:52Z), policy prefers obtaining precise ephemeris before committing to a maneuver. Public TLE data alone should not be used to decide a burn when time for CDM exists. Our propulsion status is verified, but the other object's maneuver capability is unknown, requiring notification.
